## PROBLEM

The runtime and specialist-definition changes cross validation, tracked execution, direct execution, pre-script discovery, and packaged-artifact boundaries. A dedicated test gate must prove the behavior before 3.21.6 publication.

## SUCCESS

Focused and package-level tests pass, an isolated consumer fixture proves arbitrary pack-name resolution in both Specialists spawn paths, and failures are classified with exact evidence for the cross-repo live smoke.

## SCOPE

Tests covering unitAI-jndsb.11 and unitAI-jndsb.12, exact package commands, packed RC artifact, isolated HOME/prefix fixture, and bounded Specialists forensic output.

## NON_GOALS

- No Core xt launcher validation; Core task owns xt Claude/Pi live smoke.
- No npm publish/tag.
- No production consumer mutation.

## CONSTRAINTS

SCRUTINY: high. Use real filesystem fixtures and packed artifact where possible; do not mock the path resolver itself. Require positive, missing, and ambiguous cases. Capture start/resolution/failure evidence without secrets or full prompts. Clean all temporary jobs/worktrees/HOMEs.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Focused resolver/config/session/script tests pass with exact counts.
- [ ] Full Specialists unit/type/lint/build gates pass or failures are classified.
- [ ] Packed 3.21.6 artifact contains the corrected v1.9+ specialist definition.
- [ ] Isolated consumer fixture with non-default pack starts both tracked and direct execution paths.
- [ ] Missing/ambiguous project-pack cases fail before model invocation.
- [ ] Logs/forensic records identify the logical skill and bounded repo-relative resolution outcome.

## LIBRARIES

N/A — existing test runner, temp fixtures, npm pack, and Pi fake/runtime harnesses.

## OUTPUT

Exact commands/counts, artifact hash and payload evidence, path-resolution matrix, bounded logs, cleanup proof, and product/pre-existing/infrastructure failure classification.
